result.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
result.summary: Underspecified instructions leave LLM agents to decide what to do. In public services, staff write these instructions, but the agent's decisions affect residents, patients, and students. We build four expert-validated public-service scenarios with records and decision levers that can be checked in the files, collect $2{,}400$ trajectories from ten LLMs under four prompt conditions, and compare them with $1{,}000$ runs in a context-free sandbox. Agents read the records in $96.9\%$ of open-ended runs and produce an artifact or a self-chosen task in $18.7\%$; with an explicit task, $86.0\%$ produce. Domain context does not change how many runs produce ($18.7\%$ vs.\ $16.0\%$), and the production ranking of the models largely carries over (Spearman $0.79$), while the ranking by whether a model reads the records does not ($0.19$). Context cuts boundary-probing turns per run by $60\%$, and some artifacts contradict the records. We contribute a test that a public-service institution can run on its own records before procurement; its rule-based taxonomy needs no labeled data, and scenarios, code, and trajectories are released.

AI.brief_summary: 构建四个专家校验的公共服务场景，采集十种 LLM 在四种提示条件下的 2400 条轨迹并与无上下文沙盒对比，考察欠定指令下 agent 是否读取记录、是否产出任务及产物是否与记录矛盾，并提出机构可自行运行的规则式评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「agent 是否真的读取并使用给定记录、产物是否与记录冲突」的可核查检验，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据是否被实际使用或被旁路的诊断提供参照；但对象为文本记录而非 latent 状态，与主线联系需较多核查。
